Source: parent proof step 4: the cut-off homotopy Ĥ is Lipschitz, Ĥ_j are C¹ and Lipschitz with a constant independent of j, Ĥ_j → Ĥ' uniformly, and for t ∈ (0,1) and x near E (where χ̃ ≡ 1 and s(t) = t) the form (Ĥ_j^#ω)₁(t,x) is the integrand of K_jω. Self-contained; no siblings.
Notation: pr, y₀, ι, ê₀ as in the statement; J v := ι(0,v). pr(ι(t,x)) = x and (ι(t,x))₀ = t by rfl. pr and y ↦ y₀ are continuous linear with norm ≤ 1, so ‖pr y − pr y'‖ ≤ ‖y − y'‖ and |y₀ − y'₀| ≤ ‖y − y'‖. Let K := tsupport χ (compact) and B_χ := sup|χ| < ∞ (χ is continuous with compact support).
Part (A).
1. Let D := sup_K ‖G − F‖ (0 if K = ∅; finite by continuity on a compact set) and φ := χ·(G − F). Then ‖φ‖ ≤ B_χ·D everywhere, since φ = 0 off K.
2. φ is (L_χD + 2ΛB_χ)-Lipschitz. Let x, x' ∈ ℝ^P. If neither lies in K, φ(x) = φ(x') = 0. Otherwise, by symmetry, x' ∈ K. Write φ(x) − φ(x') = (χ(x) − χ(x'))·(G − F)(x') + χ(x)·((G − F)(x) − (G − F)(x')). The first term has norm ≤ L_χ‖x − x'‖·D. The second term is 0 if χ(x) = 0, and otherwise has norm ≤ B_χ·2Λ‖x − x'‖.
3. H_{F,G}(y) = F(pr y) + a(y₀)•φ(pr y). Hence ‖H_{F,G}(y) − H_{F,G}(y')‖ ≤ Λ‖y − y'‖ + |a(y₀) − a(y'₀)|·‖φ(pr y)‖ + |a(y'₀)|·‖φ(pr y) − φ(pr y')‖ ≤ (Λ + L_aB_χD + A(L_χD + 2ΛB_χ))‖y − y'‖. Conclude with LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul.
Part (B). Put H_j := H_{F_j,G_j} and V_j := G_j − F_j.
4. H_j is C¹: pr and y ↦ y₀ are continuous linear, and sums, products, scalar multiplications and compositions of C¹ maps are C¹ (ContDiff.add, ContDiff.smul, ContDiff.mul, ContDiff.comp).
5. Bounds. a is C¹ and L_a-Lipschitz, so |a'| ≤ L_a (norm_deriv_le_of_lipschitz or norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz). χ is C¹ and L_χ-Lipschitz, so ‖Dχ‖ ≤ L_χ; also Dχ = 0 off K (fderiv vanishes off tsupport). F_j, G_j are Λ-Lipschitz, so ‖DF_j‖, ‖DG_j‖ ≤ Λ. Put D₂ := sup_j sup_K ‖V_j‖, which is finite: by uniform convergence ‖V_j − (G − F)‖_∞ ≤ 2 for j ≥ j₀, so ‖V_j‖ ≤ D + 2 on K for j ≥ j₀; each of the finitely many V_j with j < j₀ is continuous, hence bounded on the compact K.
6. By the product and chain rules, DH_j(y) = DF_j(pr y)∘pr + (a'(y₀)χ(pr y))·(c ↦ c₀)⊗V_j(pr y) + a(y₀)·(Dχ(pr y)∘pr)⊗V_j(pr y) + a(y₀)χ(pr y)·(DG_j(pr y) − DF_j(pr y))∘pr. When pr y ∉ K the last three terms vanish. Hence ‖DH_j(y)‖ ≤ Λ + L_aB_χD₂ + AL_χD₂ + 2AB_χΛ =: L for all j and y. By the mean value inequality on the convex space (lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le), every H_j is L-Lipschitz.
7. For all y, ‖H_j(y) − H_{F,G}(y)‖ ≤ ‖F_j(pr y) − F(pr y)‖ + A·B_χ·(‖G_j(pr y) − G(pr y)‖ + ‖F_j(pr y) − F(pr y)‖) ≤ (1 + AB_χ)·sup‖F_j − F‖ + AB_χ·sup‖G_j − G‖ → 0. Hence H_j → H_{F,G} uniformly (Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff).
Part (C). Put z := ι(t,x).
8. The set O := {y : pr y ∈ W, y₀ ∈ (−1, 2)} is open and contains z. On O we have χ(pr y) = 1 and a(y₀) = y₀, so H'(y) = F'(pr y) + y₀•(G'(pr y) − F'(pr y)) =: H''(y). Thus H' =ᶠ[𝓝 z] H'', so H'(z) = H''(z) and DH'(z) = DH''(z) (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
9. H'' is differentiable at z with DH''(z)(c) = DF'(x)(pr c) + c₀·(G'x − F'x) + t·(DG'(x) − DF'(x))(pr c). Hence H'(z) = F'x + t(G'x − F'x). Moreover DH'(z)ê₀ = G'x − F'x, because pr ê₀ = 0 and ê₀₀ = 1. And DH'(z) ∘L J = DF'(x) + t(DG'(x) − DF'(x)), because pr(Jv) = v and (Jv)₀ = 0.
10. x' ↦ ι(t,x') equals ι(t,0) + Jx', so fderiv ℝ (x' ↦ ι(t,x')) x = J.
11. Use ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_compContinuousLinearMap, (g.compContinuousLinearMap f).curryLeft v = (g.curryLeft (f v)).compContinuousLinearMap f, and (γ ∘ L) ∘ L' = γ ∘ (L ∘L L') (ext). They give ((ω(H'z) ∘ DH'(z)).curryLeft ê₀) ∘ J = (ω(H'z).curryLeft (DH'(z)ê₀)) ∘ (DH'(z) ∘L J). By steps 9 and 10 this equals (ω(F'x + t(G'x − F'x)).curryLeft (G'x − F'x)) ∘ (DF'(x) + t(DG'(x) − DF'(x))). ∎
proof_key_steps: (A) φ = χ(G − F) is bounded and Lipschitz (case analysis on tsupport χ), and a is bounded and Lipschitz, so H = F∘pr + a(y₀)φ(pr y) is Lipschitz.
(B) H_j is C¹ and ‖DH_j‖ ≤ Λ + L_aB_χD₂ + AL_χD₂ + 2AB_χΛ with D₂ = sup_j sup_K‖G_j − F_j‖ < ∞; mean value inequality; uniform convergence from that of F_j, G_j.
(C) Near ι(t,x), H′ = F′∘pr + y₀(G′ − F′)∘pr; so DH′ê₀ = G′x − F′x and DH′∘J = DF′ + t(DG′ − DF′); curryLeft_compContinuousLinearMap gives the integrand of K.

subproblem.title: Smooth pullbacks and Cartan homotopy formula for affine homotopies of C^∞ maps (smooth case of Simon 2.25)
subproblem.statement: Conventions: ℝ^N = Euclid N and Hᵈ = μHE[d]. 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d (smooth d-forms with compact support in U) and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d; ∂X = X.boundary; X − Y is pointwise on test forms. |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector and ‖·‖ is the operator norm. M_W(X) = X.massOn W and M(X) = X.mass = M_univ(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) (contract structure IMRep U d) has μ_R = θ·Hᵈ⌞M = R.measure and R.action(γ) = ∫_M θ ξ(γ) dHᵈ for any d-form γ; X is IM if some IMRep represents it. X vanishes off E if X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω is disjoint from E. For a map Φ and a form ω, Φ^#ω(x) := ω(Φ(x)) ∘ DΦ(x) (Lean (ω (Φ x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ Φ x)). (a) Let N, N', m ∈ ℕ, Φ : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) and α a C^∞ m-form on ℝ^{N'} (IsSmoothForm α). Then Φ^#α is C^∞. (b) Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let F, G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be C^∞ and let ω be a C^∞ (k+1)-form on ℝ^P. For an (m+1)-form β (m ∈ ℕ) define the m-form K β by K β(x)(v_1, …, v_m) := ∫_0^1 β(F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)))(G(x) − F(x), A(t,x)v_1, …, A(t,x)v_m) dt, with A(t,x) := DF(x) + t(DG(x) − DF(x)). In Lean, K β x = ∫ t in 0..1, ((β (F x + t • (G x - F x))).curryLeft (G x - F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x + t • (fderiv ℝ G x - fderiv ℝ F x)). Then K ω is C^∞, and for every x: G^#ω(x) − F^#ω(x) = d(K ω)(x) + K(dω)(x). Here d = exteriorDerivative = Mathlib extDeriv, so K(dω) uses the (k+2)-form dω.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 7(b): Cartan's homotopy formula for the smooth homotopy h_j, which is Simon's derivation of 2.25 from 2.21–2.22 written on forms. Also the smoothness facts of steps 2, 4 and 7: the forms F_j^#ω and K_jω are smooth, so cut-offs of them are test forms. Mathlib conventions: extDeriv γ x v = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i (Dγ(x)[v_i])(v_0, …, v̂_i, …, v_n) (extDeriv_apply); β.curryLeft u (w) = β(Fin.cons u w); (β.compContinuousLinearMap L)(w) = β(L ∘ w). The identity of (b) was checked numerically with exactly these conventions (k = 0, 1, 2, random smooth F, G, ω on ℝ³).
Part (a).
1. The map L ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM L, from L(ℝ^N, ℝ^{N'}) to Λ^m(ℝ^{N'}) →L Λ^m(ℝ^N), is analytic (ContinuousAlternatingMap.analyticOnNhd_compContinuousLinearMapCLM univ), hence C^∞. The map x ↦ DΦ(x) is C^∞ (contDiff_infty_iff_fderiv), and x ↦ α(Φ x) is C^∞ (composition). Since Φ^#α(x) = compContinuousLinearMapCLM(DΦ(x))(α(Φ x)), Φ^#α is C^∞ by ContDiff.clm_apply. This is the argument of the accepted proof of dpf_pb_smooth_pullback_isTestForm.
Part (b). Notation: Z := ℝ × ℝ^P (product normed space) and e := (1, 0) ∈ Z. Let H : Z → ℝ^P, H(t, x) := F(x) + t•(G(x) − F(x)). For t ∈ ℝ let j_t : ℝ^P → Z, j_t(x) := (t, x), whose derivative is the constant J := ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ ℝ ℝ^P. Put V(x) := G(x) − F(x), A(t,x) := DF(x) + t•(DG(x) − DF(x)) and h(t,x) := H(t,x).
2. H is C^∞ with DH(t,x)(s, v) = s•V(x) + A(t,x)v. In particular DH(t,x) e = V(x) and DH(t,x) ∘L J = A(t,x).
3. Define the C^∞ (k+1)-form Θ on Z by Θ(z) := ω(H z) ∘ DH(z); it is smooth by the argument of step 1. Mathlib's extDeriv_pullback applies, since ω is differentiable, H is C^∞ and minSmoothness ℝ 2 ≤ ∞. It gives dΘ(z) = dω(H z) ∘ DH(z) for all z.
4. (Cartan formula for the constant field e.) Let Θ be a (k+1)-form on Z, differentiable at z. Then d(ι_eΘ)(z) + (dΘ(z)).curryLeft e = DΘ(z)[e], where ι_eΘ := (z' ↦ Θ(z').curryLeft e). Proof: curryLeft is a continuous linear map in the covector (curryLeftLI). So ι_eΘ is differentiable at z with D(ι_eΘ)(z)[u] = (DΘ(z)[u]).curryLeft e. Evaluate at w = (w_0, …, w_k) ∈ Z^{k+1}. By extDeriv_apply, d(ι_eΘ)(z)(w) = Σ_{i=0}^k (−1)^i DΘ(z)[w_i](e, w_0, …, ŵ_i, …, w_k). Also dΘ(z)(e, w_0, …, w_k) = DΘ(z)[e](w_0, …, w_k) + Σ_{i=0}^k (−1)^{i+1} DΘ(z)[w_i](e, w_0, …, ŵ_i, …, w_k), because the (k+2)-tuple (e, w) satisfies removeNth 0 = w and removeNth (i+1) = (e, w without w_i). Adding the two expressions, the sums cancel.
5. (Pull back along j_t.) For fixed t put β_t(x) := Θ(t,x) ∘ J, α_t(x) := (ι_eΘ)(t,x) ∘ J and α^d_t(x) := ((dΘ)(t,x)).curryLeft e ∘ J. Use (γ ∘ L).curryLeft u = (γ.curryLeft (L u)) ∘ L (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_compContinuousLinearMap), (γ ∘ L) ∘ L' = γ ∘ (L ∘L L') and step 2. This gives:
   β_t(x) = ω(h(t,x)) ∘ A(t,x). In particular β_1 = G^#ω and β_0 = F^#ω, since A(1,x) = DG(x), A(0,x) = DF(x), h(1,x) = G x and h(0,x) = F x.
   α_t(x) = (ω(h(t,x)).curryLeft V(x)) ∘ A(t,x) =: κ(t,x), the integrand of Kω.
   α^d_t(x) = (dω(h(t,x)).curryLeft V(x)) ∘ A(t,x) =: κ^d(t,x), the integrand of K(dω), using step 3.
6. ι_eΘ is C^∞ and j_t is affine, so extDeriv_pullback gives dα_t(x) = d(ι_eΘ)(t,x) ∘ J. By the chain rule, t ↦ Θ(t,x) ∘ J has derivative DΘ(t,x)[e] ∘ J, because γ ↦ γ ∘ J is continuous linear. Compose the identity of step 4 at z = (t,x) with J. For all t and x this gives
   ∂_t β_t(x) = dα_t(x) + κ^d(t,x).   (∗)
7. (Smoothness of K.) Lemma: let Y be a Banach space and f : ℝ × ℝ^P → Y C^∞. Then x ↦ ∫_0^1 f(t,x) dt is C^∞, with derivative ∫_0^1 D_x f(t,x) dt, where D_x f(t,x) := Df(t,x) ∘L J. Proof by induction on n ∈ ℕ of the claim: for every Banach space Y (all at once) and every C^∞ f, x ↦ ∫_0^1 f(t,x) dt is C^n. Write ∫_0^1 as the integral over Ioc 0 1 for the finite measure volume.restrict (Ioc 0 1) (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le).
   n = 0: fix x₀; f is bounded on the compact set [0,1] × closedBall(x₀, 1), and dominated convergence gives continuity (intervalIntegral.continuous_parametric_intervalIntegral_of_continuous).
   n → n+1: apply hasFDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_of_fderiv_le at x₀ with neighbourhood ball(x₀, 1) and F'(x, t) := D_x f(t,x). The bound sup{‖D_x f(t,x)‖ : t ∈ [0,1], ‖x − x₀‖ ≤ 1} < ∞ holds by continuity on a compact set. This gives HasFDerivAt (x ↦ ∫ f(t,x) dt) (∫ D_x f(t,x₀) dt) x₀. The map (t,x) ↦ D_x f(t,x) is C^∞ with values in L(ℝ^P, Y), so by the induction hypothesis its integral is C^n. Then contDiff_succ_iff_hasFDerivAt gives C^{n+1}. Hence C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ⊤ from all n).
   The integrand κ of Kω is C^∞ on ℝ × ℝ^P: (t,x) ↦ ω(h(t,x)) is C^∞; V and A are C^∞ because F, G, DF and DG are; (γ, u) ↦ γ.curryLeft u is a continuous bilinear map; and (γ, L) ↦ γ ∘ L is C^∞ as in step 1. Hence Kω is C^∞, which is the first conclusion of (b). Likewise κ^d is C^∞, since dω is.
8. (Integrate (∗).) Fix x. t ↦ β_t(x) is C^∞, and its derivative ∂_tβ_t(x) is continuous in t. The fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt) gives G^#ω(x) − F^#ω(x) = β_1(x) − β_0(x) = ∫_0^1 ∂_tβ_t(x) dt = ∫_0^1 dα_t(x) dt + ∫_0^1 κ^d(t,x) dt. Both integrands are continuous (intervalIntegral.integral_add). The last integral is K(dω)(x) by definition.
9. ∫_0^1 dα_t(x) dt = d(Kω)(x). By step 7, D(Kω)(x) = ∫_0^1 D_xκ(t,x) dt. extDeriv γ x = alternatizeUncurryFin (Dγ(x)), and alternatizeUncurryFin is a continuous linear map (alternatizeUncurryFinCLM), so it commutes with the integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm or intervalIntegral_comp_comm). Since α_t = κ(t, ·), dα_t(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(D_xκ(t,x)). Hence d(Kω)(x) = ∫_0^1 dα_t(x) dt, and step 8 gives G^#ω(x) − F^#ω(x) = d(Kω)(x) + K(dω)(x). ∎
proof_key_steps: (a) Φ^#α = compContinuousLinearMapCLM(DΦ)(α∘Φ) with compContinuousLinearMapCLM analytic, so ContDiff.clm_apply gives smoothness.
Write the affine homotopy as H(t,x) = F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) on Z = ℝ × ℝ^P and Θ := H^#ω; extDeriv_pullback gives dΘ = H^#(dω).
Cartan formula for the constant field e = (1,0): d(ι_eΘ) + ι_e dΘ = DΘ[e], by expanding extDeriv_apply.
Pull back along j_t(x) = (t,x) (extDeriv_pullback again) to get ∂_t(h_t^#ω) = d(κ(t,·)) + κ^d(t,·), where κ, κ^d are the K-integrands.
Smoothness of x ↦ ∫_0^1 f(t,x) dt by induction with hasFDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_of_fderiv_le; then K ω is C^∞.
Integrate in t (FTC) and commute d with ∫dt (alternatizeUncurryFin is a CLM) to get G^#ω − F^#ω = d(Kω) + K(dω).

subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and Hᵈ = μHE[d]. Write ι(t,x) := (t, x_1, …, x_P) ∈ ℝ^{P+1} (Lean WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x))), pr(y) := (y_1, …, y_P) ∈ ℝ^P (Lean WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp y))) and ê₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1. Let M ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel and countably k-rectifiable with H^k(M) < ∞. Then there is a Borel set C ⊆ ι((0,1) × M) ⊆ ℝ^{P+1} with three properties. (1) C is countably (k+1)-rectifiable. (2) H^{k+1}⌞C = ι_*(L¹⌞(0,1) ⊗ H^k⌞M), i.e. μHE[k+1].restrict C = ((volume.restrict (Ioo 0 1)).prod (μHE[k].restrict M)).map ι. (3) For H^{k+1}-a.e. y ∈ C and every linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P: if M has approximate tangent space Q at pr(y) (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M (pr y) Q), then C has approximate tangent space span(insert ê₀ (J''Q)) = ℝê₀ ⊕ J(Q) at y, where J v := ι(0, v).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 3(ii)–(iv). There M is parametrized by bi-Lipschitz pieces, and the injective area formula on the pieces gives H^{k+1}⌞((0,1) × G_i(B_i)) = L¹⌞(0,1) ⊗ H^k⌞G_i(B_i), with Jacobian JĜ_i(t,u) = JG_i(u); (0,1) × M is rectifiable with tangent planes ℝe₀ ⊕ T_xM. Here the cylinder is taken over the union M' of the pieces, with H^k(M ∖ M') = 0, which makes the product-null lemma 3(i) unnecessary; the tangent planes come from the accepted piece lemma instead of blow-ups. Siblings used: codim1_lura_gram_area_formula (GA), dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces (BP) and dpf_approxTangent_ae_bilipschitz_piece (PT). For f : ℝ^m → ℝ^Q let Jf(x) := √det(⟨Df(x)e_a, Df(x)e_b⟩)_{a,b} with e_a = EuclideanSpace.single a 1. (GA) says Jf is Borel. It also says ∫⁻_{f(s)} g dH^m = ∫⁻_s ofReal(Jf)·(g∘f) dλ for every g : ℝ^Q → [0,∞] and every Borel s on which f is injective and differentiable with injective derivative. SimonGMT's Lipschitz area formula is outside the import closure, so (GA) is used instead.
Notation: ι(t,x) := toLp(Fin.cons t (ofLp x)) ∈ ℝ^{P+1}, pr(y) := toLp(Fin.tail(ofLp y)) ∈ ℝ^P and y₀ := ofLp y 0. By definition pr(ι(t,x)) = x and (ι(t,x))₀ = t (rfl). ê₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 = ι(1,0) and J v := ι(0,v); J is a linear isometry, and ⟨ι(s,x), ι(s',x')⟩ = ss' + ⟨x,x'⟩, so ê₀ ⊥ J(ℝ^P). For a subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P put Q̂ := span(insert ê₀ (J''Q)) = span{ê₀} ⊔ J(Q). For b ∈ ℝ^{k+1} write b₀ := ofLp b 0 and tail b := toLp(Fin.tail(ofLp b)) ∈ ℝ^k, and put π(b) := (b₀, tail b) ∈ ℝ × ℝ^k.
Part A (one piece). Let G : ℝ^k → ℝ^P be L-Lipschitz and B ⊆ ℝ^k Borel, with G injective on B, differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B, and H^k(G(B)) < ∞ (this holds for the pieces in Part B, since G_i(B_i) ⊆ M). Claim: H^{k+1}⌞ι((0,1) × G(B)) = ι_*(L¹⌞(0,1) ⊗ H^k⌞G(B)).
A1. π is a measurable equivalence that maps Lebesgue measure on ℝ^{k+1} to vol_ℝ ⊗ vol_{ℝ^k}. To see this, compose three measure-preserving equivalences (MeasurePreserving.prod and comp): ofLp : ℝ^{k+1} → (Fin (k+1) → ℝ) (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp); MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) 0, which is z ↦ (z 0, Fin.tail z); and toLp on the second factor (PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp). Similarly (t,x) ↦ ι(t,x) is a continuous linear equivalence ℝ × ℝ^P ≃ ℝ^{P+1}, hence a measurable embedding.
A2. Let Ĝ : ℝ^{k+1} → ℝ^{P+1}, Ĝ(b) := ι(b₀, G(tail b)), and B̂ := π⁻¹((0,1) × B), which is Borel. Then Ĝ(B̂) = ι((0,1) × G(B)), and Ĝ is injective on B̂. Ĝ is Lipschitz, since ‖Ĝ b − Ĝ b'‖² = |b₀ − b'₀|² + ‖G(tail b) − G(tail b')‖² ≤ max(1, L)²‖b − b'‖². Hence Ĝ is continuous and measurable.
A3. Let b ∈ B̂ and u := tail b. Since Ĝ = ι ∘ (id × G) ∘ π, the chain rule shows Ĝ is differentiable at b with DĜ(b)c = ι(c₀, DG(u)(tail c)) = c₀ê₀ + J(DG(u)(tail c)). DĜ(b) is injective: ι(c₀, DG(u) tail c) = 0 forces c₀ = 0 and DG(u)(tail c) = 0, so tail c = 0 and c = 0.
A4. Use the standard bases (e_a) of ℝ^{k+1} and (e'_a) of ℝ^k. Then DĜ(b)e_0 = ê₀ and DĜ(b)e_{a+1} = J(DG(u)e'_a). Let Γ̂ := (⟨DĜ(b)e_a, DĜ(b)e_c⟩) and Γ := (⟨DG(u)e'_a, DG(u)e'_c⟩). By the inner product formula: Γ̂_{00} = 1, Γ̂_{0,c+1} = Γ̂_{c+1,0} = 0 and Γ̂_{a+1,c+1} = Γ_{ac}. Laplace expansion along row 0 (Matrix.det_succ_row_zero) gives det Γ̂ = det Γ. Hence JĜ(b) = JG(tail b) on B̂.
A5. H^k⌞G(B) is a finite measure, since H^k(G(B)) < ∞ (isFiniteMeasure_restrict). So Tonelli (Measure.prod_apply, lintegral_prod) applies to vol⌞(0,1) ⊗ H^k⌞G(B).
A6. Compare both measures on a Borel set S (Measure.ext), with S_t := {x : ι(t,x) ∈ S}.
   Left side: μHE[k+1](S ∩ Ĝ(B̂)) = ∫⁻_{Ĝ(B̂)} 1_S dH^{k+1}.
   (GA) for Ĝ on B̂ gives ∫⁻_{B̂} ofReal(JĜ)·1_S∘Ĝ dvol, which by A4 equals ∫⁻_{B̂} ofReal(JG(tail b))·1_S(ι(b₀, G(tail b))) db.
   Change variables along π (A1, MeasurePreserving.setLIntegral_comp_preimage); the integrand is measurable because JG is Borel by (GA)(i) and G is continuous. Then apply lintegral_prod: the result is ∫⁻_{(0,1)} ∫⁻_B ofReal(JG(u))·1_S(ι(t, G u)) du dt.
   (GA) for G on B with g := 1_S(ι(t, ·)) shows the inner integral equals H^k(G(B) ∩ S_t).
   Right side: (vol⌞(0,1) ⊗ H^k⌞G(B))(ι⁻¹S) = ∫⁻_{(0,1)} H^k(G(B) ∩ S_t) dt (Measure.map_apply; Measure.prod_apply with A5). Both sides agree.
Part B (the cylinder). Let M be as in the statement.
B1. Apply (BP) to M. It gives Lipschitz G_i : ℝ^k → ℝ^P, Borel B_i ⊆ ℝ^k and m_i > 0 with m_i‖a − a'‖ ≤ ‖G_i a − G_i a'‖ on B_i, G_i differentiable with injective derivative on B_i, and pairwise disjoint Borel sets G_i(B_i) ⊆ M. Moreover H^k(M ∖ M') = 0 for M' := ⋃_i G_i(B_i). Each G_i is injective on B_i.
B2. Put C := ι((0,1) × M') = ⋃_i C_i with C_i := ι((0,1) × G_i(B_i)). These are pairwise disjoint Borel sets, since ι is a measurable embedding. C is Borel and C ⊆ ι((0,1) × M).
B3. (Conclusion (1).) C ⊆ ⋃_i range Ĝ_i with Ĝ_i(b) := ι(b₀, G_i(tail b)), and each Ĝ_i is Lipschitz (A2). So C is countably (k+1)-rectifiable: in the definition take M₀ = ∅ and the parametrizations Ĝ_i.
B4. (Conclusion (2).) Let S be Borel. Then:
   μHE[k+1](S ∩ C) = Σ_i μHE[k+1](S ∩ C_i) (disjoint union);
   = Σ_i ∫_{(0,1)} H^k(G_i(B_i) ∩ S_t) dt (Part A for G_i, B_i, using C_i = Ĝ_i(B̂_i); H^k(G_i(B_i)) ≤ H^k(M) < ∞);

So for a.e. b ∈ B̂_i, C has approximate tangent space range DĜ_i(b) at Ĝ_i(b).
   (c) For a.e. b ∈ B̂_i, tail b satisfies (a). The exceptional set lies in π⁻¹((0,1) × Z) with Z ⊆ B_i Lebesgue-null, which is null since π is measure preserving and (vol ⊗ vol)((0,1) × Z) = 0.
   (d) Let b satisfy (b) and (c); put u := tail b and y := Ĝ_i(b), so pr y = G_i u. Let Q be any subspace with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M (pr y) Q. By uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) and (a), Q = range DG_i(u). By A3, range DĜ_i(b) = span{ê₀} ⊔ J(range DG_i(u)). For ⊆ use DĜ_i(b)c = c₀ê₀ + J(DG_i(u) tail c); for ⊇ use ê₀ = DĜ_i(b)e_0 and J(DG_i(u)w) = DĜ_i(b)(ι_k(0,w)). Also span{ê₀} ⊔ J(Q) = span(insert ê₀ (J''Q)) = Q̂, because J''Q is the image of a subspace under a linear map (Submodule.span_insert, Submodule.map). Hence C has approximate tangent space Q̂ at y, by (b).
   (e) Every y ∈ C lies in some C_i = Ĝ_i(B̂_i). The set of y where (d) fails lies in ⋃_i Ĝ_i(Z_i) with Z_i ⊆ B̂_i Lebesgue-null, by (b) and (c). Cut M into disjoint pieces G_i(B_i) up to an H^k-null set and set C := ι((0,1) × ⋃ G_i(B_i)); C is Borel, ⊆ ι((0,1)×M), and covered by the Lipschitz maps Ĝ_i, hence rectifiable.

subproblem.title: Analytic toolkit (compactly vanishing IM representations, Hadamard and frame action bounds, Lipschitz-preserving mollification, smooth cut-offs) and the Lipschitz push-forward operator on compactly vanishing IM currents (Simon 2.29, 3.9)
subproblem.statement: Conventions: ℝ^N = Euclid N and Hᵈ = μHE[d]. 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d (smooth d-forms with compact support in U) and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d; ∂X = X.boundary; X − Y is pointwise on test forms. |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector and ‖·‖ is the operator norm. M_W(X) = X.massOn W and M(X) = X.mass = M_univ(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) (contract structure IMRep U d) has μ_R = θ·Hᵈ⌞M = R.measure and R.action(γ) = ∫_M θ ξ(γ) dHᵈ for any d-form γ; X is IM if some IMRep represents it. X vanishes off E if X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω is disjoint from E. For a map Φ and a form ω, Φ^#ω(x) := ω(Φ(x)) ∘ DΦ(x) (Lean (ω (Φ x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ Φ x)). (i) Let P, k ∈ ℕ. Let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) (domain univ) be represented by an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in univ, and let E ⊆ ℝ^P be compact with X vanishing off E. Then H^k(M ∖ E) = 0, M(X) = μ_R(ℝ^P) and μ_R(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞. Moreover R.action(γ) = R.action(γ') for all k-forms γ, γ' (arbitrary functions ℝ^P → Λ^k) with γ = γ' on E. (ii) (Hadamard) For all N, m ∈ ℕ, every m-covector α on ℝ^N and all v_1, …, v_m ∈ ℝ^N: |α(v_1, …, v_m)| ≤ |α|·∏_i‖v_i‖. (iii) Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep of degree k in any U ⊆ ℝ^P with μ_R(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞, let γ be any k-form and c ≥ 0. Assume that for H^k-a.e. x ∈ M, |γ(x)(τ_1, …, τ_k)| ≤ c for every orthonormal family τ in ℝ^P. Then |R.action(γ)| ≤ c·μ_R(ℝ^P) (real number via ENNReal.toReal). (iv) For all N, N' ∈ ℕ, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 and every Λ-Lipschitz F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} there are C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) Λ-Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} (j ∈ ℕ) with F_j → F uniformly on ℝ^N. (v) For every compact E ⊆ ℝ^P there are a C^∞ function χ : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, and an open W ⊇ E with χ = 1 on W. (vi) (Push-forward operator.) Assume (IPF), the conclusion of the frozen statement of dor_lmb_fcd_im_pushforward, which the parent obtains by applying that declaration to the antecedent (IMS). (IPF) says the following. Let N, N', k ∈ ℕ and let R be an IMRep of degree k in univ ⊆ ℝ^N with μ_R(ℝ^N) ≠ ∞. Then there is Y : (ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}) → 𝒟_k(ℝ^{N'}) with two properties. (a) For every Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 and every Λ-Lipschitz F, Y(F) is IM. Moreover, for every sequence of C¹ Λ-Lipschitz maps F_j → F uniformly and every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}), R.action(F_j^#ω) → Y(F)(ω). (b) Y(F) = Y(F') whenever F, F' are Λ-Lipschitz and F = F' H^k⌞R.carrier-a.e. Then for every P ∈ ℕ there is an operation push : ∀ k, (ℝ^P → ℝ^P) → 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) → 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) with the following property. Let k ∈ ℕ, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, F Λ-Lipschitz, E ⊆ ℝ^P compact, and X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) IM and vanishing off E. Then: (P1) push k F X is IM. (P2) push k F X = push k F' X for every Λ-Lipschitz F' with F = F' on E. (P3) Let F_j be C¹ Λ-Lipschitz maps with F_j → F uniformly on ℝ^P, let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P), and let η_j ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) be test forms with η_j(x) = F_j^#ω(x) for all x ∈ E. Then X(η_j) → push k F X(ω). (P4) M(push k F X) ≤ Λ^k·M(X). (P5) push k F X vanishes off F(E). The Lean statement is the conjunction (i) ∧ (ii) ∧ (iii) ∧ (iv) ∧ (v) ∧ ((IPF) → (vi)).

Source: parent proof (dor_lmb_fcd_pushforward_homotopy). Part (i) is its step 1(a)–(c). Parts (ii)–(iii) are the Hadamard bound and the estimate (★) in its notation paragraph. Part (iv) is the mollification of step 2, and part (v) is the cut-off functions ζ and χ̃ of steps 2, 4 and 7. Part (vi) is steps 1–2 (push via IPF, Char-push), step 5(3) (locality) and step 6 (integrality, mass bound via (★), vanishing off F(E)) for push. Siblings used: dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support (C1), covectorEuclideanNorm_gram_bounds (GB) and dpf_exists_orthonormal_frame_det_gram (GF). ContDiffBump.normed is outside the import closure of GMT.Ch07.Submission, so bumps are normalized by hand, as in the accepted proof of cmcs_lipschitz_smoothing.
Part (i). Let R = (M, θ, ξ) and W₀ := ℝ^P ∖ E, which is open because E is compact, hence closed.
1. By (C1) with U = univ (open) and T = X: X.massOn W = μ_R(W) for every open W.
2. X.massOn W₀ is the supremum of ofReal(X ω) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ k W₀. Every such ω has tsupport ω ⊆ W₀, so tsupport ω is disjoint from E and X ω = 0. Thus the supremum is taken over a subset of {0}, and X.massOn W₀ = 0 (sSup_le). By step 1, μ_R(W₀) = 0.
3. R.measure = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ, so μ_R(W₀) = ∫⁻_{M∩W₀} θ dHᵏ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_apply for the measurable W₀). θ is ℕ-valued with θ(x) > 0, i.e. (θ(x) : ℝ≥0∞) ≥ 1, for x ∈ M. Hence Hᵏ(M ∩ W₀) = ∫⁻_{M∩W₀} 1 dHᵏ ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩W₀} θ dHᵏ = 0 (setLIntegral_mono; θ is measurable). As M ∖ E = M ∩ W₀, Hᵏ(M ∖ E) = 0.
4. M(X) = X.massOn univ = μ_R(univ), by step 1 with W = univ.
5. μ_R(univ) = μ_R(E) + μ_R(W₀) = μ_R(E) = ∫⁻_{M∩E} θ dHᵏ. This is ≠ ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult with K = E (compact, ⊆ univ).
6. Let γ = γ' on E. The integrands x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(γ x) and x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(γ' x) agree at every x ∈ E. Their difference set lies in ℝ^P ∖ E, which is (Hᵏ⌞M)-null by step 3: (Hᵏ⌞M)(Eᶜ) = Hᵏ(M ∩ Eᶜ) = 0. So the integrands agree (Hᵏ⌞M)-a.e., and integral_congr_ae gives R.action γ = R.action γ'. No integrability is needed.
Part (ii).
7. If (v_1, …, v_m) is linearly dependent, then α(v) = 0 (AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent applied to α.toAlternatingMap). The right side is ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg, norms ≥ 0).
8. If v is linearly independent, (GF) gives an orthonormal σ and A_{ab} = ⟨σ_a, v_b⟩ with det(⟨v_a, v_b⟩) = (det A)² and |det A| ≤ ∏‖v_a‖. By (GB)(1), |α(v)| ≤ |α|·√det(⟨v_a, v_b⟩) = |α|·√((det A)²) = |α|·|det A| ≤ |α|·∏‖v_a‖ (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs; |α| ≥ 0).
Part (iii). Let μ := Hᵏ⌞M and f(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(γ x).
9. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there are Q and an orthonormal τ : Fin k → ℝ^P (from IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q) such that ξ(x)(β) = β(τ) for all β, or ξ(x)(β) = −β(τ) for all β. Combine this with the hypothesis. For μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(γ x)| = |γ(x)(τ)| ≤ c, hence ‖f(x)‖ = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(γ x)| ≤ c·θ(x).
10. x ↦ c·θ(x) is μ-integrable: θ is measurable and ∫⁻ θ dμ = μ_R(univ) < ∞ (withDensity_apply on univ).
11. MeasureTheory.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le needs integrability only of the majorant; it gives |R.action γ| = ‖∫ f dμ‖ ≤ ∫ cθ dμ = c·∫ θ dμ. Finally ∫ θ dμ = (∫⁻ θ dμ).toReal = μ_R(univ).toReal (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae; θ is the cast of a natural number).
Part (iv). Fix N, N', Λ and F.
12. For j ∈ ℕ put r_j := 1/(j+1). Let b_j be the ContDiffBump centred at 0 ∈ ℝ^N with rIn = r_j/2 and rOut = r_j. It is C^∞ with 0 ≤ b_j, support b_j = ball(0, r_j), and compact support. I_j := ∫ b_j dvol > 0, because b_j ≥ 0 is continuous and integrable and its support is a ball of positive volume (integral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg). Put ψ_j := I_j⁻¹·b_j. Then ψ_j is C^∞, ψ_j ≥ 0, ∫ψ_j = 1, support ψ_j ⊆ ball(0, r_j), and ψ_j has compact support.
13. Define F_j := ψ_j ⋆ F, i.e. F_j(x) = ∫ ψ_j(y)•F(x − y) dy (Mathlib convolution ψ_j F (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume). F is continuous, hence locally integrable, so HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left shows F_j is C^∞.
14. F_j is Λ-Lipschitz. Fix x, x'. The integrands y ↦ ψ_j(y)•F(x − y) and y ↦ ψ_j(y)•F(x' − y) are integrable (continuous, supported in the compact support of ψ_j). So F_j(x) − F_j(x') = ∫ ψ_j(y)•(F(x − y) − F(x' − y)) dy, and ‖F_j(x) − F_j(x')‖ ≤ ∫ ψ_j(y)·Λ‖x − x'‖ dy = Λ‖x − x'‖ (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, ∫ψ_j = 1). Conclude with LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul.
15. For every x and y ∈ ball(x, r_j), dist(F y, F x) ≤ Λ·r_j. Apply Mathlib dist_convolution_le with support ψ_j ⊆ ball(0, r_j), ψ_j ≥ 0, ∫ψ_j = 1, F strongly measurable, z₀ := F x and ε := Λ·r_j. It gives dist(F_j x, F x) ≤ Λ·r_j for every x. Since Λ·r_j → 0, F_j → F uniformly (Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff).
Part (v). Fix a compact E.
16. Let V := thickening 1 E (open, hence measurable). Let ψ be as in step 12 with radius 1/2: C^∞, ψ ≥ 0, ∫ψ = 1, support ψ ⊆ ball(0, 1/2), compact support. Put χ := ψ ⋆ 1_V, the convolution with the indicator of V. This indicator is bounded and measurable, hence locally integrable, so χ is C^∞ by HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left.
17. χ(x) = ∫ ψ(y)·1_V(x − y) dy ∈ [0, ∫ψ] = [0, 1].
18. Let W := thickening (1/2) E. It is open, and E ⊆ W (self_subset_thickening; trivial if E = ∅). Let x ∈ W and z ∈ ball(x, 1/2). Then infDist(z, E) ≤ infDist(x, E) + dist(z, x) < 1, so z ∈ V and 1_V(z) = 1. dist_convolution_le with ε = 0 and z₀ = 1 gives χ(x) = 1.
19. Let infDist(x, E) ≥ 3/2, or E = ∅. Then every z ∈ ball(x, 1/2) has z ∉ V, so 1_V = 0 there, and dist_convolution_le with ε = 0, z₀ = 0 gives χ(x) = 0. Hence support χ ⊆ cthickening (3/2) E, which is compact (IsCompact.cthickening in the proper space ℝ^P). So χ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.of_support_subset_isCompact or closure argument).
Part (vi). Assume (IPF) and fix P. Parts (i)–(iv) above are used.
20. (Definition.) Call X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) admissible if some IMRep R in univ represents X with μ_R(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞. For admissible X, choose (Classical.choose) such an R_X. Then use (IPF) with N = N' = P and R = R_X to choose Y_X satisfying (a) and (b). Define push k F X := Y_X(F) for admissible X, and push k F X := 0 otherwise.
21. Fix k, Λ, a Λ-Lipschitz F, a compact E and an IM X vanishing off E. By part (i) any IMRep of X has finite measure, so X is admissible. Let R := R_X = (M, θ, ξ) and Y := Y_X. By (i): H^k(M ∖ E) = 0, M(X) = μ_R(ℝ^P) < ∞, and R.action γ = R.action γ' whenever γ = γ' on E.
22. (P1): Y(F) is IM by (IPF)(a).
23. (P2): {x ∈ M : F x ≠ F' x} ⊆ M ∖ E is H^k-null, so F = F' H^k⌞M-a.e., and (IPF)(b) gives Y(F) = Y(F').
24. (P3): X(η_j) = R.action(η_j), because R represents X. This equals R.action(F_j^#ω) by step 21, since η_j = F_j^#ω on E. Finally R.action(F_j^#ω) → Y(F)(ω) by (IPF)(a).
25. By (iv) choose C^∞, hence C¹ (ContDiff.of_le), Λ-Lipschitz F_j → F uniformly. Then push k F X(ω) = lim_j R.action(F_j^#ω) for every ω, by (IPF)(a).
26. (P4): Let ω satisfy |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y. For all j, x and orthonormal τ: ‖DF_j(x)‖ ≤ Λ (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz), so by (ii) |F_j^#ω(x)(τ)| = |ω(F_j x)(DF_j(x)τ_1, …, DF_j(x)τ_k)| ≤ |ω(F_j x)|·∏‖DF_j(x)τ_i‖ ≤ Λ^k. By (iii) with c = Λ^k, |R.action(F_j^#ω)| ≤ Λ^k·μ_R(ℝ^P).toReal. Let j → ∞ (step 25): push k F X(ω) ≤ Λ^k·M(X).toReal. Hence ofReal(push k F X(ω)) ≤ Λ^k·M(X), using M(X) < ∞, ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal and (Λ : ℝ≥0∞)^k = ofReal(Λ^k). Taking sSup over massAdmissibleOn univ k univ (sSup_le) gives (push k F X).mass ≤ Λ^k·M(X).
27. (P5): Let tsupport ω ∩ F(E) = ∅.
   If tsupport ω = ∅ then ω = 0, and push k F X(ω) = 0 by linearity.
   If E = ∅ then H^k(M) = 0, so every R.action vanishes (integral over a null set), and push k F X(ω) = lim 0 = 0.
   Otherwise let K := tsupport ω (closed, nonempty). e ↦ infDist(F e, K) is continuous and positive on the compact E (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos), so d := min_E infDist(F e, K) > 0. Choose j₀ with ‖F_j − F‖_∞ < d for j ≥ j₀. For j ≥ j₀ and x ∈ E, F_j x ∉ K, since otherwise infDist(F x, K) ≤ dist(F x, F_j x) < d. So ω(F_j x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and F_j^#ω(x) = 0. Hence R.action(F_j^#ω) = R.action(0) = 0 for j ≥ j₀ by step 21, and push k F X(ω) = 0. ∎

(ii) Linearly dependent: α(v) = 0. Independent: Gram bound |α(v)| ≤ |α|√det G(v) and the Gram–Schmidt frame det G(v) = (det A)², |det A| ≤ ∏|v_i|.

(v) Convolve the indicator of thickening 1 E with a bump of radius 1/2: smooth, values in [0,1], 1 on thickening 1/2 E, supported in cthickening 3/2 E.

subproblem.title: Product of an integer multiplicity representation with (0,1) (Simon 2.17–2.22, 3.2(2)): IMRep, null-set transfer and the Fubini action formula
subproblem.statement: Conventions: ℝ^N = Euclid N and Hᵈ = μHE[d]. 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d (smooth d-forms with compact support in U) and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d; ∂X = X.boundary; X − Y is pointwise on test forms. |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector and ‖·‖ is the operator norm. M_W(X) = X.massOn W and M(X) = X.mass = M_univ(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) (contract structure IMRep U d) has μ_R = θ·Hᵈ⌞M = R.measure and R.action(γ) = ∫_M θ ξ(γ) dHᵈ for any d-form γ; X is IM if some IMRep represents it. X vanishes off E if X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω is disjoint from E. For a map Φ and a form ω, Φ^#ω(x) := ω(Φ(x)) ∘ DΦ(x) (Lean (ω (Φ x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ Φ x)). Let P, k ∈ ℕ and R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep of degree k in univ ⊆ ℝ^P with μ_R(ℝ^P) ≠ ∞. Write ι(t,x) := (t, x) ∈ ℝ^{P+1} (Lean WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x))) and ê₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{P+1}. Then there is an IMRep R' of degree k+1 in univ ⊆ ℝ^{P+1} with three properties. (1) μ_{R'}(ℝ^{P+1}) ≠ ∞. (2) For every Borel S ⊆ ℝ^P with H^k(M ∖ S) = 0: H^{k+1}(R'.carrier ∖ ι([0,1] × S)) = 0. (3) For every continuous (k+1)-form β on ℝ^{P+1} with sup_y ‖β(y)‖ < ∞: R'.action(β) = R.action(x ↦ ∫_0^1 (β(ι(t,x)).curryLeft ê₀) ∘ D_xι(t,x) dt). Here D_xι(t,x) = fderiv ℝ (x' ↦ ι(t,x')) x, which is the isometric embedding J v = ι(0, v). Explicitly, R'.action β = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(∫_0^1 β₁(t,x) dt) dH^k(x) with β₁(t,x)(v_1, …, v_k) = β(ι(t,x))(ê₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) k), R.measure univ ≠ ∞ → ∃ R' : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid (P + 1))) (k + 1), R'.measure univ ≠ ∞ ∧ (∀ S : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet S → μHE[k] (R.carrier \ S) = 0 → μHE[k + 1] (R'.carrier \ ((fun p : ℝ × Euclid P => (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons p.1 (WithLp.ofLp p.2) : Fin (P + 1) → ℝ) : Euclid (P + 1))) '' (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ S))) = 0) ∧ ∀ β : DifferentialForm (Euclid (P + 1)) (k + 1), Continuous β → (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ y, ‖β y‖ ≤ C) → R'.action β = R.action (fun x => ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, ((β (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x) : Fin (P + 1) → ℝ) : Euclid (P + 1))).curryLeft (EuclideanSpace.single (0 : Fin (P + 1)) (1 : ℝ))).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ (fun x' : Euclid P => (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x') : Fin (P + 1) → ℝ) : Euclid (P + 1))) x))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 3, where the product IMRep is R̂_X = ((0,1) × M, θ∘pr₂, e₀ ∧ ξ): (iii) rectifiability, (iv) the tangent planes ℝe₀ ⊕ T_xM oriented by e₀ ∧ ξ, and (v) the action formula by Fubini. The geometry of the cylinder is the sibling dor_lmb_fcdp_cylinder (CYL).
Notation: ι(t,x) := toLp(Fin.cons t (ofLp x)) ∈ ℝ^{P+1}, pr(y) := toLp(Fin.tail(ofLp y)) ∈ ℝ^P and y₀ := ofLp y 0. By definition pr(ι(t,x)) = x and (ι(t,x))₀ = t (rfl). ê₀ := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 = ι(1,0) and J v := ι(0,v); J is a linear isometry, and ⟨ι(s,x), ι(s',x')⟩ = ss' + ⟨x,x'⟩, so ê₀ ⊥ J(ℝ^P). For a subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P put Q̂ := span(insert ê₀ (J''Q)) = span{ê₀} ⊔ J(Q). For b ∈ ℝ^{k+1} write b₀ := ofLp b 0 and tail b := toLp(Fin.tail(ofLp b)) ∈ ℝ^k, and put π(b) := (b₀, tail b) ∈ ℝ × ℝ^k.
1. (Finiteness.) θ ≥ 1 on M, so H^k(M ∩ A) ≤ μ_R(A) for Borel A. In particular H^k(M) ≤ μ_R(ℝ^P) < ∞.
2. (Cylinder.) Apply (CYL) to M = R.carrier, which is Borel, countably k-rectifiable and of finite H^k-measure. It gives a Borel C ⊆ ι((0,1) × M) such that C is countably (k+1)-rectifiable, μHE[k+1]⌞C = ι_*(L¹⌞(0,1) ⊗ H^k⌞M), and the tangent transfer (CYL)(3) holds.
3. (Borel orientation.) ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for H^k⌞M. Let ξ' be a strongly measurable function with ξ = ξ' H^k⌞M-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk). Then R.action γ = ∫_M θ ξ'(γ) dH^k for every k-form γ (integral_congr_ae). By R.orients, the set N₀ := {x ∈ M : ¬∃ Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M x Q ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ' x) Q} is H^k-null. For x ∈ M ∖ N₀, ‖ξ'(x)‖ ≤ 1, because |ξ'(x)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖∏‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).
4. (Linear maps c and Ξ.) Let c : Λ^{k+1}(ℝ^{P+1}) →L Λ^k(ℝ^P), c(β) := (β.curryLeft ê₀).compContinuousLinearMap J. It is continuous linear with ‖c‖ ≤ 1. For ζ ∈ MultiVector P k put Ξ(ζ) := ζ ∘L c ∈ MultiVector (P+1) (k+1). Ξ is continuous linear and ‖Ξ(ζ)‖ ≤ ‖ζ‖.
5. (Definition.) R' has carrier C, multiplicity θ'(y) := θ(pr y) and orientation ξ̂(y) := Ξ(ξ'(pr y)).
6. (Consequences of (CYL)(2).) Using MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map / integral_map for ι and Tonelli/Fubini on the finite product measure:
   (6a) ∫⁻_C g dH^{k+1} = ∫_{(0,1)} ∫⁻_M g(ι(t,x)) dH^k(x) dt for measurable g ≥ 0.
   (6b) ∫_C f dH^{k+1} = ∫_M ∫_{(0,1)} f(ι(t,x)) dt dH^k(x) for f integrable w.r.t. H^{k+1}⌞C (integral_prod_symm or integral_integral_swap).
   (6c) If N ⊆ ℝ^P is Borel with H^k(M ∩ N) = 0, then H^{k+1}(C ∩ pr⁻¹N) = L¹((0,1))·H^k(M ∩ N) = 0. Hence a property that holds for H^k⌞M-a.e. x holds at pr y for H^{k+1}⌞C-a.e. y (enlarge the exceptional set to a Borel null set).
7. (IMRep fields.)
   measurableSet_carrier, carrier_subset and rectifiable: (CYL) and step 2.
   measurable_mult: θ' = θ ∘ pr.
   mult_pos: y ∈ C ⊆ ι((0,1) × M) gives pr y ∈ M, so θ'(y) = θ(pr y) > 0.
   locallyIntegrable_mult: ∫⁻_{C∩K} θ' dH^{k+1} ≤ ∫⁻_C θ∘pr dH^{k+1} = ∫_{(0,1)} ∫⁻_M θ dH^k dt = μ_R(ℝ^P) < ∞, by (6a).
   aestronglyMeasurable_orient: ξ̂ = Ξ ∘ ξ' ∘ pr is strongly measurable.
8. (orients.) By (6c) applied to a Borel null set containing N₀, for H^{k+1}⌞C-a.e. y we have pr y ∉ N₀. Intersect with the almost-everywhere statement (CYL)(3). Fix such a y and put x := pr y ∈ M. There is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ' x) Q, i.e. an orthonormal τ = (τ_1, …, τ_k) with span τ = Q and ξ'(x)(α) = ±α(τ) (fixed sign).
   By (CYL)(3), C has approximate tangent space Q̂ at y.
   For β ∈ Λ^{k+1}(ℝ^{P+1}): ξ̂(y)(β) = ξ'(x)(c(β)) = ±c(β)(τ) = ±β(τ̂), where τ̂ := Fin.cons ê₀ (J ∘ τ). Here use ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply and compContinuousLinearMap_apply, with Matrix.vecCons = Fin.cons.
   τ̂ is orthonormal, since J is isometric and ê₀ is a unit vector orthogonal to J(ℝ^P). Also span τ̂ = span(insert ê₀ (J''(span τ))) = Q̂. Hence IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ̂ y) Q̂, and the orients field holds at y.
9. (Conclusion (1).) μ_{R'}(ℝ^{P+1}) = ∫⁻_C θ∘pr dH^{k+1} = μ_R(ℝ^P) < ∞, by (6a).
10. (Conclusion (2).) Let S be Borel with H^k(M ∖ S) = 0. If y ∈ C ∖ ι([0,1] × S), then y = ι(t,x) with t ∈ (0,1) and x ∈ M ∖ S, so pr y ∈ ℝ^P ∖ S. Hence H^{k+1}(C ∖ ι([0,1] × S)) ≤ H^{k+1}(C ∩ pr⁻¹(ℝ^P ∖ S)) = L¹((0,1))·H^k(M ∖ S) = 0, by (6c).
11. (Conclusion (3).) Let β be continuous with ‖β(y)‖ ≤ C_β. Put f(y) := θ'(y)ξ̂(y)(β(y)), which is measurable. For H^{k+1}⌞C-a.e. y, |f(y)| ≤ θ(pr y)·‖ξ'(pr y)‖·‖c‖·‖β(y)‖ ≤ C_β·θ(pr y), by step 3 and (6c). The bound is integrable by (6a). By (6b), R'.action β = ∫_C f dH^{k+1} = ∫_M θ(x) ∫_{(0,1)} ξ'(x)(c(β(ι(t,x)))) dt dH^k(x).
   ξ'(x) is continuous linear and t ↦ c(β(ι(t,x))) is continuous, so the inner integral is ξ'(x)(∫_0^1 c(β(ι(t,x))) dt) (ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_comp_comm). M_W(X) = X.massOn W and M(X) = X.mass = M_univ(X). An IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) (contract structure IMRep U d) has μ_R = θ·Hᵈ⌞M = R.measure and R.action(γ) = ∫_M θ ξ(γ) dHᵈ for any d-form γ; X is IM if some IMRep represents it. X vanishes off E if X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω is disjoint from E. For a map Φ and a form ω, Φ^#ω(x) := ω(Φ(x)) ∘ DΦ(x) (Lean (ω (Φ x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ Φ x)). Assume (IPF), the conclusion of the frozen statement of dor_lmb_fcd_im_pushforward, which the parent obtains by applying that declaration to the antecedent (IMS). (IPF) says the following. Let N, N', k ∈ ℕ and let R be an IMRep of degree k in univ ⊆ ℝ^N with μ_R(ℝ^N) ≠ ∞. Then there is Y : (ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'}) → 𝒟_k(ℝ^{N'}) with two properties. (a) For every Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 and every Λ-Lipschitz F, Y(F) is IM. Moreover, for every sequence of C¹ Λ-Lipschitz maps F_j → F uniformly and every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}), R.action(F_j^#ω) → Y(F)(ω). (b) Y(F) = Y(F') whenever F, F' are Λ-Lipschitz and F = F' H^k⌞R.carrier-a.e. Then for every P ∈ ℕ there is an operation homot : ∀ k, (ℝ^P → ℝ^P) → (ℝ^P → ℝ^P) → 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) → 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) with the following property. Let k ∈ ℕ, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, F, G Λ-Lipschitz, E ⊆ ℝ^P compact, and X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) IM and vanishing off E. Then: (H1) homot k F G X is IM. (H2) homot k F G X = homot k F' G' X for all Λ-Lipschitz F', G' with F = F' and G = G' on E. (H3) Let F_j, G_j be C¹ Λ-Lipschitz with F_j → F and G_j → G uniformly, ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^P), and η_j ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) test forms with η_j = K_jω on E. Here K_jω(x) := ∫_0^1 (ω(F_j x + t(G_j x − F_j x)).curryLeft (G_j x − F_j x)) ∘ (DF_j(x) + t(DG_j(x) − DF_j(x))) dt. Then X(η_j) → homot k F G X(ω). (H4) homot k F G X vanishes off {F x + t(G x − F x) : x ∈ E, t ∈ [0,1]}. (H5) For every δ ∈ ℝ with dist(F x, G x) ≤ δ on E: M(homot k F G X) ≤ ofReal(δ)·(2Λ)^k·M(X).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof steps 3–4 (the product IMRep R̂_X, the cut-off homotopy Ĥ, homot := Y_{R̂_X}(Ĥ), Char-homot), steps 5(2)–(3) (locality) and step 6 (integrality, vanishing, the mass bound 2.27 via Hadamard). Siblings used: dor_lmb_fcdp_toolkit_push (T), parts (i)–(v); dor_lmb_fcdp_product_imrep (PR); dor_lmb_fcdp_homotopy_maps (HM).
Notation: ι(t,x), ê₀, J, pr and y₀ are as in (PR) and (HM). For maps F_j, G_j put h_j(t,x) := F_j x + t(G_j x − F_j x), V_j := G_j − F_j, A_j(t,x) := DF_j(x) + t(DG_j(x) − DF_j(x)) and κ_j(t,x) := (ω(h_j(t,x)).curryLeft V_j(x)) ∘ A_j(t,x). Then K_jω(x) = ∫_0^1 κ_j(t,x) dt.
Fix P. Call X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) admissible if some IMRep in univ represents X with finite measure. For admissible X choose such an R_X = (M, θ, ξ) (Classical.choose). By (T)(i), every IM X vanishing off a compact set is admissible.
1. (Auxiliary functions.) c(t) := min(1, max(0, t)) is 1-Lipschitz, |c| ≤ 1 and c(t) = t on [0,1]. Fix a C^∞ s : ℝ → ℝ with compact support and s(t) = t on [−1,2]: take s(t) := t·φ(t), with φ the ContDiffBump on ℝ centred at 1/2 with rIn = 3/2 and rOut = 5/2. Then s and s' are continuous with compact support, so |s| ≤ S₀, |s'| ≤ S₁ and s is S₁-Lipschitz.
2. (Definition.) For admissible X let R'_X be given by (PR) for R_X, and let Y'_X be given by (IPF) for N = P+1, N' = P and R'_X (degree k+1). Let E_X := the support of the measure μ_{R_X} (closed). Put χ_X(x) := max(0, 1 − infDist(x, E_X)) if E_X ≠ ∅, and χ_X := 0 if E_X = ∅. Note that Mathlib has infDist x ∅ = 0, so the case E_X = ∅ must be treated separately. Then χ_X is 1-Lipschitz (lipschitz_infDist_pt) with values in [0,1], χ_X = 1 on E_X, and support χ_X ⊆ cthickening 1 E_X is compact once E_X is compact. Put Ĥ_{F,G,X}(y) := F(pr y) + (c(y₀)χ_X(pr y))•(G(pr y) − F(pr y)) and define homot k F G X := Y'_X(Ĥ_{F,G,X}). For non-admissible X put homot k F G X := 0.
3. Fix k, Λ, F, G, E and X as in the statement. Let R := R_X = (M, θ, ξ), R' := R'_X, Y' := Y'_X and Ĥ := Ĥ_{F,G,X}. By (T)(i): H^k(M ∖ E) = 0, M(X) = μ_R(ℝ^P) < ∞, and R.action γ = R.action γ' whenever γ = γ' on E. Next, μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ E_X) = 0 (MeasureTheory.Measure.measure_compl_support), so H^k(M ∖ E_X) = 0 because θ ≥ 1 on M. Hence R.action γ = R.action γ' whenever γ = γ' on E_X, since the integrands agree H^k⌞M-a.e. Finally E_X ⊆ E: for x ∉ E, the open set ℝ^P ∖ E ∋ x has μ_R-measure ∫⁻_{M∖E} θ = 0. So E_X is compact. If E_X = ∅ then H^k(M) = 0 and every R.action vanishes.
4. (Lipschitz.) By (HM)(A) with a = c (L_a = 1, A = 1) and χ = χ_X (L_χ = 1, compact support), Ĥ is Lipschitz. Likewise, for Λ-Lipschitz F', G', every Ĥ_{F',G',X} is Lipschitz.
5. (H1): homot k F G X = Y'(Ĥ) is IM by (IPF)(a).
6. (H2): Let F', G' be Λ-Lipschitz with F = F' and G = G' on E. For y = ι(t,x) with t ∈ [0,1] and x ∈ E we have pr y = x, so Ĥ_{F,G,X}(y) = Ĥ_{F',G',X}(y). By (PR)(2) with S := E (compact, so Borel, and H^k(M ∖ E) = 0), H^{k+1}-a.e. y ∈ R'.carrier lies in ι([0,1] × E). So the two maps agree H^{k+1}⌞R'.carrier-a.e. Both are Lipschitz (step 4; use the larger constant), so (IPF)(b) gives homot k F G X = homot k F' G' X.
7. (Characterization via R.) Claim: for C¹ Λ-Lipschitz F_j → F and G_j → G uniformly and every ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^P), R.action(K_jω) → homot k F G X(ω). Proof:
   (a) By (T)(v) applied to the compact E_X, choose a C^∞ χ̃ with compact support and 0 ≤ χ̃ ≤ 1, and an open W ⊇ E_X with χ̃ = 1 on W. χ̃ is Lipschitz: it is C¹ with compact support, so ‖Dχ̃‖ is bounded, and the mean value inequality applies. Let Ĥ* := H_{F,G} and Ĥ_j := H_{F_j,G_j} for the cut-off data (a, χ) := (s, χ̃) of (HM).
   (b) Ĥ = Ĥ* on ι([0,1] × E_X), because c(t) = t = s(t) and χ_X = 1 = χ̃ there. By (PR)(2) with S := E_X (closed, H^k(M ∖ E_X) = 0), the two maps agree H^{k+1}⌞R'.carrier-a.e. Ĥ* is Lipschitz by (HM)(A), so Y'(Ĥ) = Y'(Ĥ*) by (IPF)(b), with the larger constant.
   (c) By (HM)(B), the Ĥ_j are C¹, all L-Lipschitz for one L, and Ĥ_j → Ĥ* uniformly. Let Λ° := max(L, Lip Ĥ*). Then (IPF)(a) for R' and Ĥ* gives R'.action(Ĥ_j^#ω) → Y'(Ĥ*)(ω) = homot k F G X(ω).
   (d) β_j := Ĥ_j^#ω, β_j(y) = ω(Ĥ_j y) ∘ DĤ_j(y), is continuous: Ĥ_j is C¹, ω is continuous, and (γ, L) ↦ γ ∘ L is continuous. It is bounded by sup‖ω‖·L^{k+1}. By (PR)(3), R'.action(β_j) = R.action(x ↦ ∫_0^1 (β_j(ι(t,x)).curryLeft ê₀) ∘ D_xι(t,x) dt).
   (e) Let x ∈ W and t ∈ (0,1) ⊆ (−1,2). (HM)(C), with F' = F_j, G' = G_j, a = s and χ = χ̃, gives (β_j(ι(t,x)).curryLeft ê₀) ∘ D_xι(t,x) = κ_j(t,x). So for x ∈ W the two interval integrals over [0,1] have integrands that agree on (0,1), hence a.e. (intervalIntegral.integral_congr_ae), and are equal. Thus the form in (d) agrees with K_jω on W ⊇ E_X, and R'.action(β_j) = R.action(K_jω) by step 3.
   Combining (c)–(e): R.action(K_jω) → homot k F G X(ω).
8. (H3): X(η_j) = R.action(η_j) = R.action(K_jω), by step 3, since η_j = K_jω on E. Apply step 7.
9. By (T)(iv) choose C^∞ Λ-Lipschitz F_j → F and G_j → G uniformly, and let ε_j := sup‖F_j − F‖ + sup‖G_j − G‖ (finite for large j, tending to 0). Then homot k F G X(ω) = lim_j R.action(K_jω) for every ω, by step 7.
10. (H4): Let tsupport ω ∩ Σ = ∅, where Σ := {F x + t(G x − F x) : x ∈ E, t ∈ [0,1]} is compact, as a continuous image of [0,1] × E.
   If tsupport ω = ∅ then ω = 0 and the value is 0.
   If E = ∅ then H^k(M) = 0 and the value is lim 0 = 0.
   Otherwise d := min_{z∈Σ} infDist(z, tsupport ω) > 0. Let j satisfy ε_j < d, and let x ∈ E and t ∈ [0,1]. Then ‖h_j(t,x) − (F x + t(G x − F x))‖ ≤ (1 − t)‖F_j x − F x‖ + t‖G_j x − G x‖ ≤ ε_j < d. So h_j(t,x) ∉ tsupport ω, ω(h_j(t,x)) = 0 and κ_j(t,x) = 0. Hence K_jω = 0 on E, R.action(K_jω) = 0 for large j (step 3), and homot k F G X(ω) = 0.
11. (H5): Let dist(F x, G x) ≤ δ on E.
   If E = ∅, homot k F G X = 0 by step 10, and the bound is trivial.
   Otherwise δ ≥ 0. Let |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y, and let x ∈ E, t ∈ [0,1] and τ orthonormal. By ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply and compContinuousLinearMap_apply, κ_j(t,x)(τ) = ω(h_j(t,x))(V_j(x), A_j(t,x)τ_1, …, A_j(t,x)τ_k). Here ‖V_j(x)‖ ≤ ‖G x − F x‖ + ε_j ≤ δ + ε_j and ‖A_j(t,x)‖ ≤ (1 − t)Λ + tΛ = Λ. So (T)(ii), with k+1 vectors, gives |κ_j(t,x)(τ)| ≤ (δ + ε_j)Λ^k.
   Evaluation at τ is continuous linear, so |K_jω(x)(τ)| = |∫_0^1 κ_j(t,x)(τ) dt| ≤ (δ + ε_j)Λ^k for x ∈ E, i.e. H^k⌞M-a.e. By (T)(iii), |R.action(K_jω)| ≤ (δ + ε_j)Λ^k·μ_R(ℝ^P).toReal. Let j → ∞ (step 9): homot k F G X(ω) ≤ δΛ^k·M(X).toReal.
   Hence ofReal(homot k F G X(ω)) ≤ ofReal(δ)·Λ^k·M(X) (M(X) < ∞, ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_toReal), and taking sSup over massAdmissibleOn univ k+1 univ (sSup_le) gives (homot k F G X).mass ≤ ofReal(δ)·Λ^k·M(X). This is ≤ ofReal(δ)·(2Λ)^k·M(X), since Λ^k ≤ (2Λ)^k. ∎
proof_key_steps: homot k F G X := Y′_{R′_X}(Ĥ) with R′_X the product IMRep and Ĥ = F∘pr + c(y₀)χ_X(pr y)(G − F)(pr y), χ_X := 0 when E_X = ∅ (Mathlib infDist convention); Ĥ Lipschitz by the homotopy-maps lemma; integrality and locality from IPF via the product a.e.-containment.

Char-homot: Ĥ = Ĥ* a.e. on the product carrier, Ĥ_j → Ĥ* uniformly with uniform Lipschitz bound, the product action formula and the pulled-back integrand identity give R′.action(Ĥ_j^#ω) = R.action(K_jω) → homot(ω).
Homotopy estimates: K_jω = 0 on E for large j off the trace; Hadamard with (G_j − F_j, A_jτ) gives |R.action(K_jω)| ≤ (δ + ε_j)Λ^k M(X).
